mechanism.summary: T058: first-match traversal of a lazily quantified single-code-point atom (literal, class, dot, escape, property) tries the quantifier minimum first and steps the atom one repetition at a time only after the continuation fails, instead of scanning the atom's longest run before the first attempt. Greedy quantifiers keep the existing longest-run scan. The replace builtin's literal-source '(.+)' shortcut is removed; the general prepared global loop answers that program.
mechanism.generality: Admission depends only on the parsed atom kind and the quantifier's laziness, bounds and width in the compiled pattern: every lazy quantifier over any single-code-point atom, in every flag combination and every API (exec, test, match, matchAll, replace, split, search). No pattern source, library or benchmark shape is recognized; the change removes a source-text comparison.
semantic_risks: Lazy priority order: count min first, then min+1, ..., bounded by max and by the first atom failure
Minimum repetitions must all succeed before the first continuation attempt; a short run fails without trying the continuation
Unicode and v modes advance by code point (surrogate pairs) and legacy \u escapes can consume two units without u
Captures and backreferences inside the continuation must see the same state as before; failed attempts restore the index
Sticky and global lastIndex results and empty-match advancement must be unchanged
Removing the '(.+)' shortcut must keep replace results and lastIndex identical, including the replace-math stress case's length/OOM behavior
